title: Osteoporosis: who to screen, who to treat, and with what

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on USPSTF screening recommendations and the Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation clinician's guide. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: From what age should all women be screened for osteoporosis with a DXA scan?
questions.why: Younger postmenopausal women are screened when their fracture risk equals that of a 65-year-old, which a FRAX calculation without bone density can estimate.

questions.q: At or below what T-score is osteoporosis diagnosed?
questions.why: Between -1.0 and -2.5 is osteopenia. A hip or vertebral fragility fracture is osteoporosis regardless of the T-score.

questions.q: Which patients should be offered treatment?
a: A hip or vertebral fragility fracture
Osteopenia with a ten-year hip fracture risk of 3% or more
d: Osteopenia with no fracture and a low FRAX score
questions.why: A ten-year major osteoporotic fracture risk of 20% or more is the other FRAX threshold. Osteopenia without those is managed with calcium, vitamin D, exercise and a repeat scan.

questions.q: What is first-line drug treatment for most patients with osteoporosis?
questions.a: An oral bisphosphonate such as alendronate
questions.why: Alendronate 70 mg weekly or risedronate are the usual choices; yearly intravenous zoledronic acid for those who cannot take tablets.

questions.a: On an empty stomach with a full glass of water, staying upright for 30 minutes
questions.why: The rules prevent oesophageal injury and improve absorption, which is poor at the best of times. Oesophageal disease and inability to sit up are contraindications.

questions.q: Below what creatinine clearance is alendronate contraindicated?
questions.why: Denosumab is the usual alternative in advanced kidney disease, with attention to hypocalcaemia, which is more common and more severe there.

questions.q: After how many years of an oral bisphosphonate can a drug holiday be considered in a patient at moderate risk?
questions.why: Three years for intravenous zoledronic acid. High-risk patients, with prior fracture or a very low T-score, continue. The holiday reflects the drug's long retention in bone.

questions.q: A patient on denosumab wants to stop it. What must happen?
questions.a: Transition to a bisphosphonate; do not simply stop
d: Stop it; nothing else is needed
Taper the dose over a year
Switch to calcium and vitamin D alone
questions.why: Stopping denosumab causes rapid bone loss and clusters of vertebral fractures within a year. Doses are also never delayed by more than a few weeks.

questions.q: Which patient is a candidate for an anabolic agent such as teriparatide or romosozumab first?
questions.a: Very high fracture risk: a T-score of -3.0 or lower, or multiple or recent fractures
questions.why: Anabolic therapy is given for one to two years and must be followed by an antiresorptive, or the gains are lost.

questions.q: What total daily calcium intake, from diet and supplements together, is recommended for postmenopausal women?
questions.why: Diet is preferred; supplements only make up the shortfall. Vitamin D of 800 to 1000 international units a day goes with it.

questions.q: Which secondary causes should be looked for in a new diagnosis of osteoporosis?
questions.why: Hyperthyroidism, hypogonadism, myeloma and alcohol are also on the list. Calcium, phosphate, vitamin D, thyroid function and a full blood count are the minimum tests.

questions.q: Long-term prednisone at what daily dose, for three months or more, triggers a bone protection assessment?
questions.why: Bone loss is fastest in the first months of steroid treatment. Adults over 40 at moderate or higher risk start a bisphosphonate alongside the steroid rather than waiting for a scan.
